title: Separate diagnostic ring state from liquid colour in paired uroscopy instructions
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, SOURCE_ONLY, NOT SELECTED. Jointly recover complete conditional diagnostic statements by separating the appearance of a vessel ring from the liquid body, then requiring the same condition-to-outcome mapping across complete cases. No Voynich vessel has been identified as a urine flask and no caption ownership is supplied by this proposal.

design.primary_observation: Durham Cosin V.iv.7 f50r–59v has twenty diagnostic/prescription pages. The official catalogue distinguishes a heading about a green circle and headache from a separate liquid-colour label on the drawn bottle body, alongside its mouth label. At f45v, red connectors explicitly link groups of bottles to seven diagnostic circles. These are distinct conditional fields and explicit links, not simply a colour-word list.
design.source_status: Official custodial catalogue inspected; manuscript transcriptions and exact feature/diagnosis tables not yet collated. Describes historical diagnostic beliefs, not experimentally established medical inference.
design.joint_reading: A shared code must distinguish condition bearer (ring versus liquid body), observed state, and consequent diagnosis in complete statements. The same appearance in different compartments need not have the same diagnostic consequence. Require complete statement consumption, no occurrence-specific meanings or omitted conditions.
design.incompatible_predictions: A generic liquid-colour reading predicts one state value regardless of where the marking belongs. A compartment-sensitive conditional reading predicts distinct diagnosis clauses when ring state changes while liquid body state remains fixed. The decisive independent observation is an explicit ring/body owner distinction plus a second condition/outcome statement, not colour similarity.
design.positive_output: One complete conditional phrase with its bearer and consequence agreed across all surviving shared keys, then an independently fixed counterfactual compartment contrast or unused case predicted without refitting. Colour-only correlations and a fluent diagnosis do not qualify.
design.minimum_test: First collate one complete source pair that actually crosses ring and body states; catalogue evidence alone does not establish that such a separating pair exists. Only then nominate an admitted Voynich pair with explicit compartment ownership. No automatic new image admission or colour-decoder rerun.
missing_inputs: No admitted Voynich urine identification or explicit ring/body caption ownership.
The full historical paired case and its genuine separating condition remain to be collated.
No shared writing channel or controlled complete-statement inverse has been selected.
design.duplicate_boundary: Not a repair of COL001 colour association, top/bottom container ownership, or excluded literal medical source-copy codes. New raw question is compositional conditional field ownership and diagnosis. Requires new explicit relation evidence before any closed family can be reconsidered.
